notes:
A test loop that runs in 1.3 seconds instead of minutes, and the first slice taken off ZoneDiscoveryService with it.

FASTTESTS. A SwiftPM package whose test target compiles the pure sources directly — 47 tests in 1.3 seconds on the Mac, no simulator, no app launch. The files are SYMLINKS to the real sources (verified stored as mode 120000 in git), so the app and the fast suite compile the same bytes and cannot drift; a copy that passes while the shipping code has moved on would be worse than no test at all. It does NOT replace the hosted suite, and this release proves why: two fixture-lookup bugs shipped while the fast suite read 47/47 green, because what broke was the simulator path specifically. #filePath is a Mac path baked in at compile time and Xcode tests run inside the simulator, where /Users is unreachable. Fixture loading now tries the test bundle first and the source tree second, and the order is load-bearing.

SONOSTOPOLOGY EXTRACTED. parse, merge and applyPositionInfo — plus SonosZone, SonosGroupMember and the XML parser — moved out of ZoneDiscoveryService, which dropped from 2,377 to 2,032 lines and keeps thin wrappers. updateZoneFromPositionInfo was made PURE rather than merely moved: it now takes a zone and returns one, while the lookup and write-back that genuinely need the service stayed behind. Behaviour-preserving, confirmed by 132 hosted tests with ZonePollingTests 21/21 unchanged. This is step one of six in fZoneDiscoveryServiceDecomposition; the remaining slices are listed there, ending with the 23 PlaybackStore references that are the real state-ownership question.

AUTO-LOCK. The phone would not lock. The obvious cause was a one-way latch — isIdleTimerDisabled set in one place and cleared in four, so any hang left it stuck on. Deriving it from activeScanSourceId removes that, and on its own would have changed almost nothing: the automatic change check runs on every foreground and is dominated by the tree walk, which no tidying of the tail removes. The fix that mattered is that an AUTOMATIC check should never suppress auto-lock at all — keeping the screen awake is for a scan someone is watching. Confirmed in the room, after a false negative caused by the device being attached to Xcode, which prevents sleep regardless of what the app does.

NO-CHANGE CHECKS NO LONGER RUN THE PIPELINE. A check that filtered to zero files still ran three artwork passes, the retry scheduler and the full state sequence, because the pipeline was wired to 'a scan ran' rather than 'work was found'. Nothing is lost: pending artwork resumes on its own branch and the retrying case restarts the scheduler. The WALK still runs, because that is how it learns nothing changed. Measured in the room at planned 0 files, 0.6s. A killed automatic check also stops asking permission to resume — bPhantomScanInterruptedDialog's guard sat in the error branch, which a fresh kill only reaches one foreground later.

KNOWN LIMITATION, LOGGED NOT FIXED: bIdleTimerFollowsWedgedScanState. Deriving the timer made it honest about activeScanSourceId, but a user-initiated scan whose pipeline wedges still leaves that state set, and the screen awake with it. Closing it needs a progress timeout rather than another flag.

REPO HYGIENE. Xcode per-user state — window layout, breakpoints, scheme ordering — was tracked and rewritten on every click, leaving the tree dirty at random and breaking deploy mid-rebase. Now ignored.
